chapters.title: The graph
chapters.body:
Each file names the files it needs. The shelf walks those names and refuses a circle it cannot explain.

A missing file is a gap in the graph, not a guess.

chapters.title: One file
chapters.body:
When the walk finishes, the pages share one script. The `http` module is the part that stays outside.

What remains is the shelf itself: routes, books, and the words between them.

title: The Second Press
author: Ada Lovelace
blurb: A second edition is a diff you are willing to keep.

chapters.title: Gathering the quires
chapters.body:
The first press set the order of the chapters. The second press may only insert a leaf where the old numbers still add up.

Readers who own both editions should see the same story and a clearer margin.

chapters.title: Errata
chapters.body:
An erratum names the page, the line, and the word that replaced it. It does not rewrite the date on the title page.

The reading desk is open at this chapter.

title: Cycles and Live Bindings
author: Grace Hopper
blurb: Two modules can import each other.

chapters.title: The handshake
chapters.body:
Module A asks B for a function. Module B asks A for a constant that A has not finished writing.

The binding stays live so the later assignment is the one the call observes.

chapters.title: Who runs first
chapters.body:
Side effects run in the order the shelf first reached each file. A second import does not run them again.

If that order matters, the book says so in the margin.

title: Compiler Weather
author: Grace Hopper
blurb: Names are folded before the rain starts.

chapters.title: Forecast
chapters.body:
A constant known at the press can delete a branch. A constant known only at the desk cannot.

The forecast is written beside the code, not over it.

chapters.title: Instruments
chapters.body:
The compiler keeps a log of which names survived. The log is a chapter, not a secret.

Readers who want the raw table can ask the API for the same book.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.body:
The traveler leaves with one name and a slip of paper that says the other name is waiting inland.

Every inn along the road asks which name should be written in the book.

chapters.title: Inland
chapters.body:
Inland, the second name fits the lock. The first name still opens the letters from home.

Neither name is a lie. They are two bindings for one person.

title: Checksum Garden
author: Frances Allen
blurb: Every row of lavender has to sum to the same quiet total.

chapters.title: Rows
chapters.body:
The gardener counts leaves, not to hurry them, but to notice when a row has lost one.

A mismatch is a weed or a miscount. The book asks you to look before you pull.

chapters.title: Evening tally
chapters.body:
At dusk the totals are copied into a narrower book. The garden itself is not rewritten.

Tomorrow's row must still recognize today's sum.

title: A Server in a Bundle
author: Radia Perlman
blurb: Node's `http` module stays outside the bundle.

chapters.title: Listen
chapters.body:
The process binds `127.0.0.1` and a port. The pages are already inside the script that just started.

A request is a path, a method, and a query. The shelf answers with HTML or JSON.

chapters.title: What stays outside
chapters.body:
The bundle does not contain Node's own `http`. It calls it. That is the seam between the shelf and the machine.

Packages such as `marked` travel with the pages. The listener does not.

title: Routes and Replies
author: Radia Perlman
blurb: A path is a promise about the shape of the answer.

chapters.title: Patterns
chapters.body:
`/books/packing` is a page. `/api/books/packing` is the same book as data. The chapter path adds one more segment.

Unknown paths share one refusal, worded the same way each time.

chapters.title: Methods
chapters.body:
The shelf reads. It does not accept a body. `GET` and `HEAD` are the whole conversation.

Anything else is answered with `405` and a single plain line.

title: Margin Notes
author: Margaret Hamilton
blurb: The note in the margin is part of the program.

chapters.title: Priority
chapters.body:
When two alarms arrive together, the margin says which one may interrupt the other.

The rule is short so it can be checked by hand.

chapters.title: Display
chapters.body:
A display that hides the alarm is a different program from the one that was reviewed.

This chapter is the one currently open on the reading desk.

title: Orbital Tables
author: Katherine Johnson
blurb: A table you can recompute is a table you can trust.

chapters.title: Columns
chapters.body:
Each column names its unit before it names its numbers. A reader should not have to guess the scale.

The first column is the date. The rest are differences from a stated epoch.

chapters.title: Recompute
chapters.body:
If a later hand copies the table, the copy should meet the same totals. The original grid stays in the back of the book.

Trust here means: show the steps, then the figure.
